cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Ursula!

cue.speaker: DEATH
cue.text: Hi, again. You'll have to pardon me. I come and go. I get shy. Historically, I've been rarely met with anything other than fear or anger or ... regret and, as I'm sure you can imagine, that sort of energy gets ... taxing. So I chose long ago to abandon any material form of my own and err on the side of the covert. I prefer now to move in and out of whatever vessel inspires me because, when I'm not working, I, like you, am a watcher. I like to watch. Sometimes I am in a tree. Sometimes in a rock. In a spider. In her web. The pollen in the air. A plant. A banister. That swing-I've been that, too. Each form offering its own ... pleasures? Powers? Benefits? For instance, I inhabit a body like this if my desire is to speak and, if I have one weakness ... it's for gossip. I suspect you share it? ... I don't know what it is, but I find all creatures so interesting, their idiosyncracies, their interiorities, their secrets. Their stories. These machines of will. And, like any good gossip, I'm always wanting to talk but, you know, finding the right listeners can be a challenge. So you should know you are very special. Who is that? ... Oh, I know her...

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: What are you doing outside? It's freezing!

cue.speaker: URSULA
cue.text: Hiii.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Oh ... Okay! That's okay! Am I the first one here?

cue.speaker: URSULA
cue.text: It's not that cold. Is it? I thought we could do this on the porch.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Oh, wow. Okay. I brought snacks! Hi, honey. How are you feeling?

cue.speaker: URSULA
cue.text: Emilio is inside charging his phone.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Great! Then you can come!

cue.speaker: URSULA
cue.text: I'm feeling fine.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Ursula, you only get one twentieth reunion and I really think you're cheating yourself out of something special. Think of all the people who want to see you!

cue.speaker: URSULA
cue.text: I'm not coming.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Why would you be uncomfortable? It's just an eyepatch! There's going to be way worse accessories on display. And we're all going to be there! M.E.R.G.E.!

cue.speaker: URSULA
cue.text: I didn't want to be uncomfortable.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: He did?

cue.speaker: URSULA
cue.text: I thought Simon just cancelled?

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Hi, stranger!

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Hey!

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Yes. Thank you! Hi!

cue.speaker: URSULA
cue.text: Do you want a drink Caitlin?

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: I can't believe I haven't seen you since Kristina's wedding.

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Hi!

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: You look great.

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Me, neither. Fifteen years? What the full fuck?

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: So we're doing this outside?

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Thanks. You, too.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: That makes sense. Is this your first time seeing her since she lost the-?

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: I think she's worried about people moving things around in there.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: It's a little crazy, right? We have got to get her to come to the reunion-get her out of the house. She's basically, like, become a shut-in. Her grandmother passed like right before the quarantine and then she was just all alone in the house and then lockdown happened and then she freaking goes blind and it's horrible. I'm afraid if we don't, you know, try, she'll never, you know, reengage or something. You know what I mean? She has had like truly the worst pandemic ever-except for people who actually, you know ... died. Anyway. This is going to be fun ... How was your COVID? I don't even remember what they did over there.

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Yeah ...

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Oh my God, wait! What? When?

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Um. It was still a thing in Europe. Ironically, I got a ton of work done. I had a kid.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Way to bury the lede! Olin-na?

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Five months ago. Her name is Alena.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Oh, right. Berlin is in Germany.

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Uh, yes. It's basically Alena. But German. My partner is German.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Oh my God! Congratulations?! Gosh, how long have you been out there now?

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: That's right.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: That would be fun. Do you have pictures?

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Thirteen years. But it might be about time to move back. We'll see.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Good! They're good! Um, Brock just started law school at Madison, which is insane! And Olivia is a Junior at UVA!

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Oh! Yes! Wait, my phone is charging. Let me go grab it. How are your ... kids ... ?

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Over here. Thank you, Ursula!

cue.speaker: URSULA
cue.text: Here we go ...

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Oh my God, no! No! ... She's beautiful ...

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Here she is ...

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Ursula, did you know Emilio had a kid?

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Thanks. Made her myself. I mean, with help.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Did you bring her with you?

cue.speaker: URSULA
cue.text: He just told me.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: If I had known, I would have brought a gift. Congratulations ...

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: No, she's back in Germany. She's only five months old.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Mm! Ursula!

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Thanks.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Jungle juice?! Okay?! Mm, did Ursula tell you she took some mixology classes over the pandemic?

cue.speaker: URSULA
cue.text: It's jungle juice.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: I was trying to tell her she should really think about, you know, doing something with those classes.

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: She did ...

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: That doesn't have to be true. Michael and I were in London a few years ago and we went to this really interesting restaurant-I can't remember what it's called but it's pitch black and it's supposed to approximate the experience of being visually impaired and all of the servers and the chefs and everything are visually impaired and it was just so interesting. And I feel like there's something there. Like wouldn't it be cool if there was a speakeasy type thing that was pitch-dark and you had, you know, a bartender who was visually impaired serving your drinks? I mean, I just think that would be so interesting.

cue.speaker: URSULA
cue.text: Blind bartenders are not a thing.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: ... Are you suggesting that I was just rambling?

cue.speaker: URSULA
cue.text: Oh my God, yes. KRK.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Anyway! I can't believe Simon cancelled?

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: It was rambling. I'm pretty sure I invented the joke.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Ugh, the limo.

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: I know, so annoying. But he's offered to cover for the whole limo.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Of course I hate the fucking limo! It's embarrassing!

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Wait, you hate the limo?!

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: What? How?

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: The limo? No! It's funny!

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: But we're not teenagers anymore. Now we're just adults showing up in a limo.

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Because in high school, every stupid prom, every homecoming, we were always randomly showing up in a limo like somehow it was a thing that people did in real life.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: "Conceptual"? What does that mean?

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: But isn't the point of this dumb event reliving high school for the night? I think people will think it's funny. Maybe it is a little conceptual.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Well, you don't still live around these people. I do ...

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Don't worry about it. Listen: It's just a little nostalgia.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: So, for some of us, it may not be in our best interest to show up looking like shitheads.

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: So?

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Why?

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Okay, well talk to Kristina. Though don't people already think you're a shithead by association?

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: I just want to be mindful of other people's financial situations-like not everyone can afford a limo. And Michael was not in the group that actually stormed the capitol. And, as you well know, he and I don't necessarily share the same politics ...

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Yes, please. Are you really insulted? I'm sorry-

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: It's fine. Plus you're right. I don't want to ruin Kristina's night. I think she's actually very excited about it. Speaking of: Where the eff is she?

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: I'm sure if you wanted to drive yourself, it wouldn't be a big deal.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Uh, sort of? COVID's made things a little weird.

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Are you and Kristina still close?

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Being a doctor during the pandemic seems to have not been the greatest experience? She's definitely, like, been through some shit and I think she may have developed a drinking problem as a result?

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: How so?

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: But I'm not sure? You'll have to tell me when you see her. The last couple of times we met up for happy hour, she sort of like drank so much she ... blacked out? ... As a grown woman? ... And I was sort of like, "Huh ..." You know how there's like this behavior that you can get away with in your twenties and everyone's like, "Oh, xyz is so fun!" But then you turn this corner and suddenly it's like, "Oh she has a problem." That's kind of where I am with Kristina. I'm like, "Am I supposed to say something?" But also she's a doctor so, like, wouldn't she know better than me? But also she spent lockdown trapped in a house with Cameron and their five kids, so who am I to judge? Watching that was like ... the beginning of a podcast about murder.

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: What?

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: How long did you and Kristina "date" or whatever? I forget.

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: It's funny to think there's a bizarro multiverse in which she and I are still together.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: I know. Catholicism.

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Half of sophomore year and all of junior year? Five kids, though?

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: I have kids.

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: You know, if I thought anyone was going to have a buttload of kids, it was going to be you ...

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Uh, no one talked me out of anything. It just never happened.

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: I mean, like kids of your own. How did Michael talk you out of that?

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Wait, Ursula! You know who I just heard is going to be there tonight?

cue.speaker: DEATH
cue.text: Actually-and not to make this moment about me-what happened was, well ... one, two, three, four miscarriages over the course of as many years? If not a little less. After a while, it was difficult to keep track. And if you're not careful, the same small tragedies repeated again and again begin to take on a new shape, begin to stack up into something larger-a bigger story you start telling yourself. The story of your curse. When, honestly, what I do is not something anyone deserves. Caitlin doesn't really talk about it much, obviously, because-after the first or second, it started to feel like a character flaw. Or at least that's how her husband made her feel about it-though he enjoys his own kids from a previous marriage. He made her stop. Her nerviness was getting to be too much for him. It was turning her into a whiner. It was making her seem unattractive. And who needs their husband thinking that? And there are worse things than a dead fetus. For instance: a dead baby. For instance: a dead toddler. With a positive enough mindset, you might even find a way to consider yourself lucky. Meanwhile, she's still got her figure. Nice skin. Good teeth. There is so much to admire about the human body. Especially at this age, so noble, fighting its good fight against a certain ... softening. Your cell repair systems-my, most ancient nemeses-are long broken down. You lose those at twenty-seven. Did you know that? Is anyone here twenty-seven? ... From that point on, it's my game. Wrinkles. A little sag. A creaking in the joints. A misplaced word or two or several. From that point on, it's just me and you ... and you ... and you ... and you ... and you ... Anyway, let me stop-

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Cindy Podolski.

cue.speaker: URSULA
cue.text: Who?

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Cindy Podolski?! Come on, you remember her? She was epileptic?

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Who?

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: I think she did it for the attention. There: I said it.

cue.speaker: URSULA
cue.text: It actually happened multiple times.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: I'm saying it's suspicious that she kept going back to the dances. It's like returning to the scene of the crime.

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Are you saying she faked being epileptic?

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: There was at the fifteenth. Here she is.

cue.speaker: URSULA
cue.text: Is there going to be dancing tonight?

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: I think people are coming in from all over. I guess twenty is a big number. Which is why you need to come, Ursula! Don't you want to see Cindy seize again?!

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Oh, yeah ... I remember her... She's coming from Seattle? That's far.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: But you went to the fifteenth and the tenth and the fifth. It's going to be odd if you drop out. People are going to think you're dead! I don't want to keep having to explain to people that you're not dead!

cue.speaker: URSULA
cue.text: I'm good.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: They were fine. How come you never came?

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: How were those other reunions?

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: I ... thought it was just fun to see people ...

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: I...don't know. I was still on Facebook at the time, so I figured, like, "Why bother?" We all knew what we looked like, who had kids, who didn't have kids, who had what kind of job. I just found the idea of gathering in some random two-star Marriott to confirm all that just so tedious. I feel like before Facebook, reunions were a real encounter with the brutal beatdown of time. You just sort of showed up and had no idea who would be there or how fucked up they would look and then you realized that maybe you looked a little fucked up too and every encounter was like a whole dark ritual of the soul where each party was confronted by the specter of their own mortality, just like, "Oh shit!" I don't know. You know?

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Wait-what are you doing with my phone?

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Uh, I'm not on Facebook anymore-

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Was.

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: This is a lot of pictures of him with guns. And trucks ... Oh there's him with a gun in front of a truck ... And that's a tank. He's military?

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: I don't know. He just added me one day.

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Wait, how are you friends with Huey Michael Lewis?

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Yes? Why not? Give me my phone back!

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: And you accepted?

cards.speaker: CAITLIN

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: God, guys, remember Columbine?

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: I think that was just you.

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Man, compared to now it feels almost ... like quaint-but remember how everyone was so much nicer to Huey afterwards? Like everyone was afraid of him?

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Half of our friends were in/ JROTC-?

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: You know: spookily quiet? Kind of a recluse? Physically sort of ... elven? And, I mean, he was JROTC, which was like free revenge-training for baby psychopaths. Like, oh my God, Ryan Morgan? Do you remember him? And that guy with the birthmark on his face-Frankie ... Something. Their energy was way too dark for teenagers. And they were all in rifle club together. I mean, why was there a rifle club at our school? Like, why would you give these people access to guns? The fact you're even fake-training for a life in the military at that age clearly means there's something wrong with you.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: And Paco.

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Yeah, but that's not the same thing. Ursula only did it for a year and only for the little discount on tuition they gave you and Kristina's dad is a sergeant or whatever so she was really born into it-/ indoctrinated-

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Paco was not a psychotic?

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Okay, and Paco, but I mean, come on, hello-case in point: Paco was a psychotic.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Excuse me?

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Caitlin, are you kidding me? Paco had obvious emotional problems. Look at the way he treated you. Though, what am I even talking about? Your profound lack of boundaries back then didn't exactly help.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: The point is Huey Michael Lewis didn't shoot up the school. He actually joined the military, which was the point of JROTC-

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Oh, come on ... You know your whole obsession in high school with having a boyfriend? It just led you into these bad situations with these like messed-up, manipulative Big Chief dickhead-types and Paco was like-ugh, he was like the platonic form of this asshole. Like, he was always making you feel like shit for not doing the things he wanted you to do so then you'd do them but then he'd just basically ignore you afterwards and you'd be like crying all through lunch period and refusing to eat until everyone would have to convince you to break up but then he'd be like running around like emotionally punching lockers for the rest of the day until you'd go back to him so you could feel ... needed I guess. The cycle would just go on and on and on. But, you know, I suppose no one got enough attention at home or whatever. What? We've definitely talked about this? Like a million years ago? Do you not remember this?

cue.text: Okay.

cue.text: Okay... ?

cue.text: Really?

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Okay, Caitlin, so the military continued to be a home for an endless parade of formerly unstable youth. How is that news? I was just talking about Columbine. How do you know all this? You follow them on Instagram, too?

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: No?

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: 2010? 2011? A while ago. Anyway, I found out about that and I reached out back then. I wrote him little messages or whatever on Facebook and, when we were going back and forth, he told me there were a lot of guys over there who didn't have anyone writing to them and I started feeling guilty for some reason and, I don't know, one day I just sort of woke up in the middle of the night and friended everybody in our class who I knew or heard was over there and wrote them little notes too and I guess when everything switched over to Instagram they migrated with me. So that's why I'm friends with all those guys. Alright? Where is Kristina?

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Jesus ... When was this?

cards.speaker: CAITLIN

cards.line: Uh, not really. He moved out to California when he came back. Kristina told me he was finishing his degree. We sort of lost touch. I don't know if he even checks his messages anymore. He never posts.

cue.text: That's so weird.

cue.text: Same.

cue.speaker: DEATH
cue.text: I'd like to revise a statement from earlier. Do not get the impression that I am some sort of misanthrope. I am quite friendly. In fact, I recognized a few of you out there, in the dark. And I think some would argue that knowing me comes with certain benefits. Certain sensitivities and insights, a lucidity, a greater patience for mystery, a sense of humor. For example, Ursula. She has known me quite intimately for some time now, mostly through her grandmother's extended battles with the fickleness of the human cell. But my actual relationship with Ursula goes as far back as her ... first days of life? Her mother, the day after Ursula's delivery, stood up too quickly from her hospital bed, fell and cracked her head against the corner of a radiator. She died instantly but bled and bled and bled and the sight of all that blood sent her father running, never to return, too worried he might not ever look at his daughter and feel any other than grief. So this is why her grandmother had to raise her. Of course, when asked about the arrangement, you never lead with the details. You say simply, "My mother died." Which inevitably leads to the question, "When?" To which Ursula must reply, "Shortly after I was born." Then there's usually this pause as they wonder if she might be the culprit. Then comes the dreaded, "... How?" And, depending on the questioner, Ursula will or won't make a joke I never tire of. She goes, "Like this-" Hilarious. Because truly what difference does it make? They want to know but they really don't and, when you're in a situation like hers, you learn very early about the average person's capacity for avoiding those who seem to carry my mark. Everyone treats you differently. So, up close and personal with the power of fear, its absurdity, you develop a real sense of humor about things-about people. About life. And look at her. I think she's wonderful. I'm allowed to think people are wonderful.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: I don't want to show up to our reunion stoned!

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Caitlin, you have to have some of this or I'm not going to make it to the reunion.

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Come on. Nobody cares you're married to an ex-cop. Nobody's going to make you pee into a cup. Just have a little bit. Ursula just said it wasn't that strong. Shit. I keep forgetting about my phone. Here!

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Who is his partner?

cards.line: Francisco?

cue.speaker: KRISTINA
cue.text: Thank God. Cisco? Francisco? Paco?

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Stop it. Don't be embarrassed. It wasn't your fault.

cue.speaker: FRANCISCO
cue.text: Fuck me. Did I piss myself? Man.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Well it looks like you got your wish, Emilio!

cue.speaker: KRISTINA
cue.text: Just rest. Guys, he's disoriented. He has to regain his bearings.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Earlier, Emilio said he didn't even want Paco to be here.

cue.speaker: KRISTINA
cue.text: What?

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: You liar. You were literally standing there going "Do I feel safe?" When it's actually been you, you who we should have been safe from-with all your negativity, all your negativity all fucking night, picking at him and picking at all of us and being so judgmental-all night!

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: I did not say that!

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Oh shut up. See? This is what I'm talking about.

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Well, first of all, let me point out that I did not start this seizure. I'm not the reason this guy is sick. In fact, it sounds like the war is what fucking started these seizures, correct Kristina? And, second of all, let's not sit here and act like my magnificent powers of judgment are capable of actually making anyone do anything. I mean, I wish my judgment actually mattered here or anywhere else, but it doesn't. Why do you think I fucking got out of this stupid country?

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: You know, I actually feel sorry for you.

cue.speaker: FRANCISCO
cue.text: The thing that's here for something, for someone.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: No, you feel sorry for someone else. And I feel sorry for her, too, but she's not here right now. She's not here anymore. It's just me.

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: I actually feel sorry for you.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Prove what? If anyone's stuck, it's you. Ursula, are you coming? Everyone here's just a sad-sack loser who got stuck, that means you, too.

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Prove it.

cards.speaker: CAITLIN
cards.line: Emilio, who are you kidding? All she's done all night is show you how much she cares about you, you and your stupid art, showering you with every kind word under the sun, and what have you done? Besides shut her down. Make her feel stupid-make all of us feel stupid-when actually you're the stuck one.

cue.speaker: EMILIO
cue.text: Leave her out of this.
